finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns bool only and is not enforced; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) not called in update_doc; no ownership/editor check in update_doc; no before_request, decorator, or login_required in this file; update_title (docs.py:27) does enforce require_edit, so the omission is inconsistent. Authentication of g.user not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is called at docs.py:19 as a bare statement, so its bool result is discarded and nothing aborts. require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which does abort(403), is not called in update_doc. No before_request, decorator, or other guard exists; the only other file in the directory is none (Glob found only docs.py), so no outside guard is visible.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) without testing its return value or using require_edit, so the write at docs.py:20 runs for any caller of PUT /doc/<doc_id> who is not the owner or an editor, and the only authentication (setting g.user) is outside this file, so any authenticated low-privilege user can overwrite another user's document body.

verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (docs.py:27 calls require_edit, docs.py:12 calls can_edit, docs.py:8 does the membership test, docs.py:28 writes the title), but whether docs.py:8 is a substring match depends on doc["editors"] being a str, and nothing in the repo (DOCS is empty at docs.py:4 and never populated) shows that; if it is a list, `in` is exact membership and the finding is not exploitable.

verdict.guard_found: none. No try/except, no DOCS.get, no errorhandler or input validation exists in the directory. The only guard, require_edit (docs.py:11-13), aborts with 403 only after the KeyError at docs.py:26 has already fired for unknown IDs. docs.py:19 is a bare can_edit call whose result is discarded, so update_doc never returns 403.
verdict.reason: For PUT /doc/<id>/title, an unknown ID raises KeyError at docs.py:26 (Flask returns 500) while an existing ID that fails the check reaches abort(403) at docs.py:13 via require_edit at docs.py:27, so the 500-vs-403 existence oracle is real, but the trace step at docs.py:19 is misdescribed because that line is in update_doc, where the bare can_edit result is discarded and no 403 is produced. The missing-key and unvalidated-type 500s and stored values at docs.py:20 and 28 are real but are robustness issues rather than security findings.
